Quick answer

From 1 November 2026 a foreign adult ticket costs EGP 1,830 (about €31 at EGP 60 to the euro, 8 November 2026). The galleries open 09:00 to 18:00, and until 21:00 on Wednesdays and Saturdays. Expect the colossus of Ramesses II, the Grand Staircase, the main galleries, the complete Tutankhamun collection with the golden mask, and Khufu's boat.

The Grand Egyptian Museum (GEM) opened in November 2025 and is described as the largest museum in the world dedicated to a single civilisation. The practical questions came faster than the answers: how tickets work, what timed entry means, where Tutankhamun's mask went, and what to see in a building that holds more than 100,000 artefacts. This guide answers them, with dates on the facts that move. It is written by the people behind Sawa Tours (sawa.tours), the Egypt shared-departure platform. We have worked in Egyptian tourism since 1993, first as a guide and then running an agency.

How do I buy tickets for the Grand Egyptian Museum?

Buy online, in advance, from the official ticketing site, and pick a date and an entry window. The site visit-gem.com forwards to tickets.gem.eg, which one current guide calls the only official ticket site. Foreign visitors are told to book online because on-site sales have been suspended, so do not plan to turn up and buy at the door.

The mechanics:

  • The slot limits when you enter, not how long you stay. You choose an entry window and arrive inside it.
  • Book ahead in season. Peak slots sell out first, especially mornings and weekends, and one current guide advises two to three weeks ahead between October and April.
  • Price. A foreign adult ticket is EGP 1,830 (about €31) from 1 November 2026, up from EGP 1,570. Foreign students (aged 13 to 24, with a valid student ID) and children aged 6 to 12 pay EGP 920 (about €15). Egyptians pay a much lower rate, and children under 6 enter free.
  • One ticket covers the galleries. Admission includes the Tutankhamun galleries and Khufu's boat; there is no separate Tutankhamun ticket.
  • Guided ticket. The museum sells its own guided-tour ticket in English or Arabic at a higher price. It is a museum-led group product, not a private guide.
  • Non-refundable and non-transferable. Settle your date before you pay.

Grand Egyptian Museum opening hours and timed entry, explained

The GEM runs two clocks: the wider complex (outside areas, shops, cafés) opens at 08:30, and the galleries keep their own hours.

Standard days Wednesdays and Saturdays
Galleries 09:00 to 18:00 09:00 to 21:00
Wider complex 08:30 to 19:00 08:30 to 22:00
Last tickets sold 17:00 20:00

Hours change in Ramadan and on public holidays, so check the official site for the week you travel.

The late nights are the quietest hours on offer. On Wednesdays and Saturdays the galleries stay open to 21:00, when most day-tour groups have left. The early slot is the calmest of the standard hours. The hours to avoid are weekend middays, when the slot system is fullest. The museum has reported around 19,000 visitors on busy days, so even a quiet hour is relative.

Where is Tutankhamun's mask now?

Tutankhamun's golden mask is at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza, in the Tutankhamun galleries. The mask left the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir with the rest of the boy king's tomb collection, more than 5,000 objects excavated from the Valley of the Kings in 1922, and at the GEM the collection is displayed together for the first time.

The galleries are reached from Gallery 7 and arranged in five sections: discovery, lifestyle, rebirth, funeral and identity. Allow 60 to 90 minutes, and more if you read the cases. Tutankhamun's mummy is not in the museum: it remains in his tomb in the Valley of the Kings.

The old Egyptian Museum in Tahrir is still open, with its own collections, including the Narmer Palette. Foreign-adult admission there is EGP 550 (about €9). For a first visit, the GEM replaces the Tahrir highlights, and "the Tutankhamun museum in Cairo" now means the GEM.

The Grand Egyptian Museum highlights: what to see, and in what order

The building rewards a route. This one follows the visitor's path from the entrance upwards:

  1. The colossus of Ramesses II. The 3,200-year-old granite statue of the great king greets you in the entrance atrium, the first "how is it that big?" moment.
  2. The Grand Staircase. A broad ascent lined with more than 60 monumental pieces, arranged by era. There are 148 steps (with a moving walkway beside them for anyone who prefers it), and the top has views of the Giza pyramids.
  3. The main galleries. Twelve main galleries run in chronological order from the earliest dynasties to the Greco-Roman period. Pick one thread (kingship, craft, the afterlife) rather than trying to see everything.
  4. The Tutankhamun galleries. The complete tomb collection, with the golden mask as the centrepiece.
  5. Khufu's boat. The 4,600-year-old funerary boat of the Great Pyramid's builder was moved from beside the pyramid in 2021 and hangs in its own hall. A second boat is being reassembled in front of visitors, a process reported to take up to four years from December 2025. The boat is no longer on the plateau, so do not walk out there looking for it.

Time budget: 2.5 to 3 hours covers this route at a comfortable pace; enthusiasts should give it four or more, and the late-night days exist for exactly that.

Getting there and pairing it with the Pyramids

The GEM stands in Giza, about 2 km from the Pyramids plateau. From central Cairo, an Uber or Careem ride typically takes 30 to 45 minutes depending on traffic. There is no official shuttle and no direct public transport, so most visitors arrive by ride-hailing app or with a tour.

The two sites pair into one classic Cairo day: the Pyramids at opening while the desert is cool, lunch, then the GEM's air-conditioned galleries in the afternoon. Practical notes: photography, food and access

  • Photography. Personal photos and video are allowed. Flash, tripods, selfie sticks and drones are not, and commercial use needs written permission. Rules can differ by gallery, so follow the signs.
  • Food. There are several places to eat inside the complex, so plan lunch there rather than leaving. Outside food and drink are not allowed.
  • Access. The Grand Staircase has a moving walkway beside it and a wheelchair platform. The building is vast, so wear comfortable shoes.
  • Bags. Security screening runs at the entrance, and bags over 40 × 40 cm go to the cloakroom. Travel light, especially if you are pairing the day with the plateau.
  • Pairing with the plateau. The Pyramids site now runs through a new visitor centre and main entrance on the Cairo to Fayoum road, so allow a little extra time to get in.

The short version

Book the Grand Egyptian Museum online on the official site: choose an entry window, pay EGP 1,830 (about €31) as a foreign adult, and arrive for the 09:00 opening, or on a Wednesday or Saturday evening for the quiet version. Walk the route: the Ramesses II colossus, the Grand Staircase, the main galleries, the complete Tutankhamun collection with the golden mask, and Khufu's boat. Two and a half to three hours is comfortable, and the museum pairs with a Pyramids morning into the best single day in Giza. The full plan is in our one-day guide, or book the combined day tour from €71, as listed in November 2026.

faq.q: How do I buy tickets for the Grand Egyptian Museum?
faq.a: Online, on the official ticketing site (visit-gem.com, which leads to tickets.gem.eg). Choose a date and an entry window, and pay EGP 1,830 (about €31) for a foreign adult from 1 November 2026. Book days or, in high season, weeks ahead: mornings and weekends sell out first. Tickets are non-refundable and non-transferable.

In the Tutankhamun galleries at the Grand Egyptian Museum in Giza. The complete tomb collection of more than 5,000 objects moved there from the Egyptian Museum in Tahrir and is displayed together for the first time.

faq.q: What are the GEM opening hours?
faq.a: The galleries open 09:00 to 18:00, and until 21:00 on Wednesdays and Saturdays. The wider complex opens from 08:30. The last tickets are sold at 17:00 on standard days and 20:00 on late days. Hours change in Ramadan, so check the official site.
Yes, at peak times. The timed-entry system caps each window, and mornings and weekends go first. Book on the official site as far ahead as your plans allow, and do not rely on buying at the door.

faq.q: Is Khufu's boat at the Grand Egyptian Museum?
faq.a: Yes. Khufu's 4,600-year-old boat was moved from beside the Great Pyramid and is displayed at the GEM in its own hall. A second boat is being reassembled in public view. The old boat museum on the plateau no longer holds the boat.

faq.q: How much time do you need at the Grand Egyptian Museum?
faq.a: Two and a half to three hours covers the colossus, the Grand Staircase, a thread through the main galleries and the Tutankhamun collection. Enthusiasts should budget four or more. Paired with the Pyramids in one day, plan the plateau for the morning and the GEM after lunch.

faq.q: Should I see the GEM or the Egyptian Museum at Tahrir?
faq.a: For a first visit, the GEM: it holds Tutankhamun's complete collection and the grand scale. The Tahrir museum is still open with a large historic collection, and is a good second visit.
